content.text: FacebookLog InLog InForgot Account?Apollo 11 Astronauts' Salaries and Benefits During the 1969 Moon LandingSummarized by AI from the post belowSpace Hipsters · JoinSteve Russo · July 31, 2024 · Shared with Public groupI was doing some research for the 50th Anniversary of the first Moon landing and found some interesting info from NASA on the salary of the Apollo 11 crew.The Apollo 11 Astronauts were not paid big salaries. I have put the "worded" salaries in there too so no one thinks my numbers were a typo.Armstrong was a civilian so his yearly salary in 1969 was $20,000.00 (twenty thousand). Aldrin and Collins were in the Air Force so their annual salary in 1969 was $16,000.00 (sixteen thousand) each. Since the Federal Government considered the Moon Landing as a "trip", the Apollo 11 Astronauts were paid a "per-diem" of $8.00 (eight dollars) a day for room, board, and meals. However, since all of that was supplied by NASA on board the spacecraft, each astronaut received a "salary" of just over $33.00 (thirty three dollars) for their trip to the Moon! Today's Astronauts have a starting annual salary of around $81,000.00, (eighty one thousand), and they top off at $146,000.00 (one hundred fourty six thousand). Most Astronauts make more money on the "talk-circuit" after they retire, some charging over $30,000.00 (thirty thousand) for an hour-long talk!All reactions:179 comments4 sharesLikeCommentShareMost relevant Joe HowleyOf course the 1960s astronauts also got plenty of fringe benefits, including payment from LIFE Magazine for interviews/articles (I believe this payment was more than their official paychecks from NASA) and they also got abundant "freebies" from Houston… See more1y2Patti Goff MitchellI saw a listing of Apollo engineer salaries in 1969 and the amounts are similar, meaning it was a good salary in 1969.1y1Kevin P.
